name: Santiago Wells
life: “I still remember spending one shared journey quietly after a family illness.” On Wednesday, near the market by Market Flats, Santiago often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I used to travel in complete silence. I asked the others to let me have one quiet morning a week.
appearance: Santiago has a long face and high cheekbones. Look for a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an unlined tan jacket with a folded shopping list secured by a miniature clip. In conversation Santiago looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Santiago is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To claim one quiet ride each week.
family: Nadia Black is Santiago’s cousin. Santiago sets the time to leave. Nadia picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Nadia says, “I am tired of brides apologizing to the glass.”
connections: Diego Medina. One passenger hears a quiet journey while a resident sees the missing car in the street.
